challenges.headline: Editing totals directly
challenges.premise: Users overwrite the reported total with a new number.
challenges.alternative: Record each change as a separate, attributed, reversible adjustment line, so the total remains the sum of its entries plus adjustments and the original stays visible.
challenges.consequence: An overwritten total silently disagrees with its own source data. The report stops tying out, an auditor cannot see what changed, and exports already sent become wrong without anyone knowing.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with Finance that edits are adjustments, not overrides, before any design work.

challenges.headline: Editing any period freely
challenges.premise: Totals can be edited whenever a user wants, whatever the state of the period.
challenges.alternative: Allow edits only in open periods, and route corrections to a closed period as adjustments in the next open period. Reopening a closed period would be a rare, logged, approved act.
challenges.consequence: Editing closed figures invalidates every export and report already filed or sent from that period.
challenges.recommendation: Agree with Finance which period states allow edits and how a closed-period correction is handled.

challenges.headline: Building before checking existing features
challenges.premise: Editing and exporting are new capabilities to build.
challenges.alternative: The platform already has period review and close and an export to the accounting system. The need may be met by adding adjustment entries to them and a finance-facing view or file of the same data.
challenges.consequence: A separate new export duplicates the existing one and creates two versions of the figures to reconcile.
challenges.recommendation: Check what the current export and review features cover, and why they fall short, before scoping.

complexity_reasons: export as a versioned contract with its consumer
briefs.cost_driver: the adjustment, approval and audit model on derived totals
risks: A change to how figures are derived in the shared aggregation layer shifts every other report, export and dashboard built on it.
If edits are built as overrides, reports stop tying to source data and the gap surfaces at audit time.
Corrections after an export or close leave previously sent exports stale unless they are tracked and flagged.
The export format may be rejected by the accounting system, or may differ per client, which multiplies the work.
Rights are easy to forget: seeing, adjusting and closing are separate, and segregation of duties changes the approval flow.

opportunities.text: Make adjustment entries a first-class line type in the existing aggregation, so budget vs. actual, period close and exports all read the same adjusted and unadjusted figures.
Treat the export as a versioned, retained snapshot, which also gives a basis for flagging exports made stale by later corrections.
Reuse the platform's approval-circuit pattern for adjustment approval rather than building a bespoke one.

page.title: Edit totals as adjustments, then export
page.recommendation: Decide that edits to reported totals are recorded as separate, attributed adjustments rather than overwritten numbers, and that the export is built on the existing accounting export. We recommend settling a few rules with Finance before any build starts.
page.why: A reported total is the sum of its underlying entries. Overwriting it makes the report disagree with its own data and leaves exports already sent silently wrong. An adjustment keeps the original visible, shows who changed what and why, and lets Finance see figures with and without corrections. The platform already has period close and an accounting export, so extending them is likely cheaper than building something parallel.
page.cost_and_risk: The main cost is the adjustment, approval and audit model on top of derived figures. The risk that matters most is that a change to the shared aggregation layer shifts every other report and export built on it, and that a correction after close leaves sent exports stale.

open.question: Should an edit be a separate adjustment line, or replace the displayed number?
open.would_change: A replacement is a different, riskier build that decouples the report from its data and complicates audit.

open.question: May closed periods be corrected, and if so as an adjustment in the next period or by reopening?
open.would_change: Reopening requires controlled, logged approval and invalidates prior exports, which sizes the workflow.

open.question: Is the export a file for people or a feed to the accounting system, and does the format differ per client?
open.would_change: A fixed-format feed, especially per client, raises the cost sharply compared with a spreadsheet file.

open.question: What goes wrong today, and how are totals corrected now?
open.would_change: If the cause is bad source data, fixing it there may replace much of this build.

open.question: Is something in the existing export or period close usable or deliberately set aside?
open.would_change: Extending it could remove a large part of the build and sets the budget.

open.question: Who may see, make, approve and close adjustments, and must these be different people?
open.would_change: Segregation of duties adds an approval step and scoping by entity.

open.question: Is a full change history for auditors required, including which exports predate a change?
open.would_change: If so, the audit trail and stale-export tracking become part of the first release.

challenges.headline: Editing the total directly
challenges.premise: Users should be able to edit a reported total itself.
challenges.alternative: A total is the sum of underlying entries. Recording a correction as a separate, attributed, reversible adjustment entry keeps the sum tying out, and the report can show actuals and actuals plus adjustments side by side.
challenges.consequence: A plain override replaces the value so it silently disagrees with its own source entries. The report stops reconciling, and an auditor cannot see what changed, by whom or why.
challenges.recommendation: Agree with Finance that every edit is an adjustment entry, not an override, before any design starts.

challenges.headline: Edits without a period rule
challenges.premise: Users can edit totals whenever they need to.
challenges.alternative: Allow free adjustment only while the period is open. After close, route corrections to an adjustment in the next open period, with re-opening or restatement as a separate, controlled and logged act.
challenges.consequence: Editing a closed period changes figures already exported or filed. Every earlier export and sent report becomes stale without anyone being told.
challenges.recommendation: Decide which corrections must reach a closed period and what happens to exports already sent.

challenges.headline: Is a new export needed?

challenges.alternative: The platform already exports to the accounting system and has period review and close. Extending that export with the adjusted figures, or a second format on the same snapshot mechanism, may cover the need at lower cost.
challenges.consequence: A parallel export duplicates the format contract, the retention of sent versions and the rounding rules, and gives two sources for the same figures.
challenges.recommendation: Compare what the finance team needs with what the current export carries before specifying anything new.

challenges.headline: Editing the total directly
challenges.premise: Users should be able to edit a reported total as if it were a stored value.
challenges.alternative: A total is the sum of its entries, so the correction can be a visible, attributed adjustment line with a reason. The total then still adds up and the change can be reversed or approved.
challenges.consequence: A replaced value silently stops tying to its own entries. Finance or an auditor then finds a report that disagrees with the system, with no record of who changed it or why.
challenges.recommendation: Agree with the client before build that edits are adjustment entries, not overrides. If an override is truly needed, require a visible marker, a reason and an approval.

page.title: Editing totals and exporting for finance
page.recommendation: Decide how a reported total may be changed. We recommend that users correct totals through visible, attributed adjustment entries with a reason, never by overwriting the figure, and that finance receives adjusted figures by extending the export you already have rather than building a new one.
page.why: A reported total is the sum of its underlying entries. Overwriting it makes the report disagree with its own data, and nobody can say who changed it or why. An adjustment keeps the total tied to its source, can be approved or reversed, and gives an auditor a clear record. Your module already exports to the accounting system, so extending that path avoids building and maintaining a second one.
page.cost_and_risk: The main cost is the adjustment and period-close model together with the audit trail, which is far cheaper to build in than to add later. The risk that matters most is changes to closed or already-exported periods, which make figures finance has already received stale.

open.question: When you say 'edit a total', do you want a visible correcting line that keeps the total tied to its entries, or a replaced figure?
open.would_change: If a plain replacement is truly required, the build is simpler but needs a clear override marker, a reason and approval, and reports will no longer reconcile on their own.

open.would_change: If edits after close are needed, a restatement path and flagging of outdated exports come into scope, which raises cost noticeably.
